ITEC 310 · INTERNET OF THINGS · WEEK 6

Connecting Smart Objects

Today, we will learn how smart objects connect to sensors using GPIO and communicate wirelessly using Wi-Fi and BLE. Then, we will explore MQTT and how it helps us monitor and control devices.

CLO 4 · CLO 58 Learning Sections10 Interactive MCQs
SECTION 01 / 08CONNECTING SMART OBJECTS

Let’s Remember

In the Internet of Things (IoT), a smart object is a physical device that can collect information, process it, and communicate with other devices. Some smart objects can also perform actions automatically. For example, in a smart classroom, a door sensor detects when someone opens the door. The controller receives this information and can send it to a dashboard so the teacher knows the door is open.

Next topic →
SECTION 02 / 08CONNECTING SMART OBJECTS

GPIO: Local Connections

GPIO stands for General Purpose Input/Output. GPIO pins allow a controller to connect directly to sensors and other electronic components. An input pin receives information from a sensor or button. An output pin sends a signal to control a component such as an LED or buzzer. For example, when a classroom door opens, the door sensor sends a signal to the controller's input pin. The controller can then activate a buzzer through an output pin.

Next topic →
SECTION 03 / 08CONNECTING SMART OBJECTS

Wi-Fi and BLE: Wireless Communication

Smart objects sometimes need to communicate without cables. Wi-Fi allows a controller to connect to a local network and possibly the Internet. For example, a controller can send classroom temperature readings to a dashboard using Wi-Fi. BLE stands for Bluetooth Low Energy. It is useful when a device needs to communicate with a nearby smartphone while using relatively little power.

Next topic →
SECTION 04 / 08CONNECTING SMART OBJECTS

What Is MQTT?

MQTT stands for Message Queuing Telemetry Transport. It is a lightweight communication protocol commonly used in IoT. MQTT allows smart devices to send messages to other devices or applications through an MQTT broker. For example, a controller receives a classroom temperature reading of 32°C from a sensor and publishes it. The MQTT broker receives the message and forwards it to the subscribed dashboard.

Next topic →
SECTION 05 / 08CONNECTING SMART OBJECTS

Main Components of MQTT

MQTT communication involves a publisher, broker, subscriber, topic, and payload. The publisher sends a message to the broker. The broker distributes the message to subscribers interested in its topic. The topic identifies the message channel, while the payload contains the actual information. For example, a controller publishes a temperature reading of 32 to the topic classroom/temperature. A dashboard subscribed to that topic receives the reading.

Next topic →
SECTION 06 / 08CONNECTING SMART OBJECTS

How MQTT Works: Temperature Monitoring

Imagine a classroom temperature sensor measures 32°C. The controller reads the temperature and connects to an MQTT broker through the network. The controller publishes the reading to the topic classroom/temperature. The broker checks which applications subscribe to this topic and forwards the message to them. Finally, the teacher sees the temperature on the dashboard.

Next topic →
SECTION 07 / 08CONNECTING SMART OBJECTS

MQTT Can Also Control Devices

MQTT is not only used for monitoring; it can also be used to control devices. For example, a teacher wants to turn ON a classroom fan using a dashboard. The dashboard publishes the command ON to the topic classroom/fan/control. The MQTT broker forwards the command to the controller, which is subscribed to that topic. The controller receives the command and controls the fan using suitable switching hardware.

Next topic →
SECTION 08 / 08CONNECTING SMART OBJECTS

Why Do We Need MQTT?

Imagine a university wants to display the same classroom temperature on a teacher's laptop, smartphone, and university dashboard. Without a messaging system, managing communication with several applications can become complicated. MQTT makes this easier. The controller publishes the temperature reading once to the broker, and the broker distributes it to all subscribers interested in the topic.
